Overlays: spatial layers that change the rules

Source: R/overlays.R
overlay.Rd

An overlay is a map layer that changes what the zone allows wherever it applies. The spatial data is supplied at run time under the overlay's layer name; the rulebook holds only what the overlay does.

Usage

overlay(
  id,
  type = c("height", "height_surface", "exclusion", "parameters", "flag"),
  layer,
  combine = NULL,
  value = NULL,
  value_field = NULL,
  value_map = NULL,
  floor_value = NULL,
  filter = NULL,
  removes = NULL,
  buffer = NULL,
  applies_to_zones = NULL,
  parameters = NULL,
  additions = NULL,
  enabled = TRUE,
  precedence = 0,
  label = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  notes = NULL
)

Arguments

id

Identifier.

type

What the overlay does:

  • "height": a height limit, a fixed value or read from value_field (optionally through value_map);

  • "height_surface": a raster surface of maximum height (airport surfaces, viewshafts, sunlight planes);

  • "exclusion": land under the overlay is taken out of the buildable area (hazards, designations, tree protection);

  • "parameters": replaces or adjusts named zone parameters, given as zone_changes();

  • "flag": tags the site and changes nothing.

layer

Name of the layer supplied at run time.

combine

How the overlay's value combines with the zone's (see Combining rules below). Defaults: "cap" for heights, "replace" for parameters.

value, value_field, value_map

Fixed value, or the attribute holding it, or a named list mapping attribute codes to values.

floor_value

A height always allowed regardless of the surface, so the effective height is max(surface, floor_value).

filter

Named list: attribute to accepted values, applied when the layer is read.

removes

For exclusions: "all" (every building) or "residential" (dwellings only).

buffer

For exclusions: distance (m) to buffer the features by, or the name of an attribute holding it (e.g. a tree protection radius).

applies_to_zones

Zone keys the overlay applies in; NULL for all.

parameters

For type = "parameters": a zone_changes().

additions

A zone_changes() whose setbacks are added to the zone's own instead of replacing them (e.g. an extra yard).

enabled

Whether a run uses the overlay unless told otherwise.

precedence

Tie-break between overlays: higher wins.

label, source, notes

Description and citation.

Value

A list with class plancap_overlay.

Combining rules

Every applicable rule produces a limit, and each declares how its limit combines with the others:

  • "cap": the most restrictive wins (the default for limits);

  • "replace": replaces the zone's value even if more permissive;

  • "floor": a minimum entitlement that cannot be taken away;

  • "add" / "multiply": bonuses and percentage adjustments.

Evaluation order is fixed: zone, then areas (precincts), then overlays, then bonuses, then entitlements.

See also

add_overlay()

Examples

overlay("height_control", "height", layer = "height_areas",
        value_field = "max_height_m", combine = "replace",
        source = "Planning maps, height control")
#> $type
#> [1] "height"
#> 
#> $layer
#> [1] "height_areas"
#> 
#> $combine
#> [1] "replace"
#> 
#> $value_field
#> [1] "max_height_m"
#> 
#> $enabled
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $precedence
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $source
#> [1] "Planning maps, height control"
#> 
#> attr(,"id")
#> [1] "height_control"
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "plancap_overlay"
overlay("flood", "exclusion", layer = "flood_hazard", source = "Rule 9.2")
#> $type
#> [1] "exclusion"
#> 
#> $layer
#> [1] "flood_hazard"
#> 
#> $removes
#> [1] "all"
#> 
#> $enabled
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $precedence
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $source
#> [1] "Rule 9.2"
#> 
#> attr(,"id")
#> [1] "flood"
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "plancap_overlay"
